introduction: agent-fox's agentrun package closes every phase's system prompt with a tools note. This spec makes that note render every registered tool's PromptGuidelines. In phases that have both a shell and the built-in file tools, the note also tells the model to read, search, find and list with the built-in tools and to keep the shell for git and the build/test toolchain. The execute description gets the same steer.

glossary.built-in file tools: Here, the four read/search/list tools read_file, search_files, find_files and list_files.
glossary.guidelines section: The part of the tools note that starts with the heading line "Tool guidelines:" and is followed by one "- " bullet per rendered guideline.
glossary.preference line: The sentence in the tools note that names which built-in file tool to use for reading, searching, finding and listing, and limits the shell to git (and, in writing phases, building, formatting and testing).
glossary.registered set: The core.Tool values a phase registers with the agent after SelectTools, including phase-specific submit_* tools.
glossary.search-over-execute guideline: The text "Prefer search_files over execute+grep: it respects .gitignore and returns structured matches." Taken from tools.SearchOverExecuteGuideline if AgentKit exports it, otherwise from a local constant with the same text.
glossary.shell tool: A tool whose name is in agentrun.ShellTools: execute, run_command or powershell.
glossary.tools note: The text toolsNote(registered) in internal/agentrun/phase.go returns, which newAgent appends to core.AgentConfig.SystemPrompt. It starts with "Your tools are exactly: …".
glossary.writing phase: A phase whose registered set contains write_file or edit_file.

requirements.title: Tool guidelines are rendered into the tools note
requirements.rationale: agent-fox always sets a custom system prompt, so AgentKit's prompt.Build never emits the guidelines block. The tools note is the only place they can reach the model.

criteria.condition: at least one tool in the registered set has a PromptGuidelines entry whose trimmed text is non-empty
criteria.action: append, after the "Your tools are exactly: …" sentence, a guidelines section made of the heading line "Tool guidelines:" followed by one line "- <trimmed guideline>" per rendered guideline
criteria.contract: The returned string contains "Tool guidelines:" exactly once, after "Your tools are exactly:", and contains every non-empty guideline of every registered tool, built-in and submit_* tools alike

criteria.action: visit tools in ascending sorted-name order, the same order as the tool list, and emit each tool's guidelines in their declared PromptGuidelines order

criteria.condition: a guideline is the empty string or contains only whitespace
criteria.action: skip that guideline and emit no bullet for it
criteria.contract: No "- " bullet line with empty or whitespace-only text appears in the returned string

criteria.condition: a guideline's trimmed text exactly equals the trimmed text of a guideline already emitted, whether on the same tool or another
criteria.action: skip the repeated guideline so only its first occurrence is emitted
criteria.contract: Each distinct guideline text appears in the guidelines section exactly once

criteria.condition: no registered tool has a non-empty guideline, or the registered set is empty
criteria.action: omit the guidelines section entirely
criteria.contract: The returned string does not contain "Tool guidelines:"; the rest of the note matches the pre-existing tool list and shell sentences

requirements.title: Search-over-execute guidance
requirements.rationale: AgentKit's source could not be read, so it is unknown whether search_files carries the line itself. Adding it by condition and de-duplicating works either way.

criteria.guard: the registered set contains at least one shell tool
criteria.action: include the search-over-execute guideline in the guidelines section exactly once, whether or not search_files' own PromptGuidelines already contains it

criteria.condition: the registered set lacks search_files or lacks every shell tool
criteria.action: not add the search-over-execute guideline
criteria.contract: strings.Count(note, searchOverExecuteText) == 0 for a set without a shell, because SelectTools has removed it from search_files' guidelines there; with a shell but without search_files it does not appear unless another registered tool declares it

requirements.title: Explicit preference for the built-in file tools
requirements.rationale: An execute description that lists cat and grep reads like an invitation to use them. One explicit line steers the model to the structured tools.

criteria.condition: the registered set contains a shell tool
criteria.guard: it contains at least one of read_file, search_files, find_files, list_files
criteria.action: emit exactly one preference line naming only the registered tools among those four, in the fixed order and phrasing "Read files with `read_file`, search with `search_files`, find files with `find_files` and list directories with `list_files`", with the clauses for absent tools omitted, followed by a clause limiting the shell under its registered name
criteria.contract: The note contains the preference line once; a built-in file tool that is not registered is not named in it

criteria.condition: the registered set is a writing phase's set (contains write_file or edit_file) and has a shell tool and a built-in file tool
criteria.action: end the preference line with the clause "use `<shell>` only for git and for building, formatting and testing", where <shell> is the registered shell tool's name
criteria.contract: For {read_file, search_files, write_file, execute} the note contains "use `execute` only for git and for building, formatting and testing"

criteria.condition: the registered set has a shell tool and a built-in file tool but neither write_file nor edit_file
criteria.action: end the preference line with the clause "use `<shell>` only for git" and no building/testing wording
criteria.contract: For {read_file, search_files, execute} the note contains "use `execute` only for git" and does not contain "building, formatting and testing"

criteria.action: place the preference line after the "Your tools are exactly: …" sentence and before the "Tool guidelines:" heading

criteria.condition: the registered set has a shell tool but none of read_file, search_files, find_files, list_files
criteria.action: omit the preference line
criteria.contract: The note contains no "Read files with" / "search with" / "list directories with" sentence

requirements.title: Phases without a shell keep their current guidance

criteria.condition: no shell tool is in the registered set
criteria.action: keep the existing sentence "There is no shell: read with the file tools, and do not call `bash`, `execute` or `run_command`." and emit neither the preference line nor the search-over-execute guideline

criteria.condition: SelectTools is called with names that contain no shell tool
criteria.action: keep dropping every PromptGuidelines entry that contains "execute", so that none of those entries appears in the guidelines section toolsNote renders for that set
criteria.contract: The rendered note for a no-shell selection contains no guideline line that mentions execute; TestSelectToolsDropsExecuteGuidelinesWithoutAShell keeps passing

requirements.title: The execute description discourages reading files through the shell
requirements.rationale: The description must still list exactly what the guard allows. An added sentence steers the model without breaking that.

criteria.condition: SelectTools is called with names that include execute
criteria.guard: the names include read_file or search_files
criteria.action: add to execute's phase-specific description, in both the read-only and the writing variant, a sentence saying not to use cat, head, tail, grep or rg to read or search repository files, and to use the selected built-in tools, which respect .gitignore and return structured results, instead
criteria.contract: The selected execute tool's Description contains "cat", "grep" and "rg" in the discouraging sentence and names `read_file` only if it was selected and `search_files` only if it was selected

criteria.condition: SelectTools is called with execute but with neither read_file nor search_files
criteria.action: leave execute's description without the discouraging sentence
criteria.contract: The Description equals the current describeForPhase output for that readOnly flag and program list

criteria.action: keep the "The only programs allowed are: <programs>" text of execute's description generated from the same programs slice the guard enforces, unchanged by the added sentence

requirements.title: Deterministic tools note
requirements.rationale: Byte-identical prompts keep provider prompt caching effective and runs reproducible.

criteria.action: for any registered set, return byte-identical output on repeated calls and for any input permutation of that set, with no dependence on map-iteration order, time or randomness
criteria.contract: toolsNote(s) == toolsNote(s) == toolsNote(permute(s)) for every generated set s

requirements.title: One change applies to every runner phase

criteria.action: send the provider a system prompt equal to the phase's System text followed by toolsNote of that phase's registered set, so the guidelines section, the preference line and the search-over-execute guideline reach the model
criteria.contract: The system prompt the faux provider receives for a phase registering read_file, search_files, execute and a submit_* tool with guidelines contains "Tool guidelines:", that submit tool's guideline, the search-over-execute guideline once and the preference line

criteria.action: implement requirements 1 to 6 only in internal/agentrun, with no change to the prompt text in codefix, codeimpl, specgen, issuetriage or internal/conform, and no change to tool allowlists, guard rules or internal/repomap Intro text

requirements.title: Documentation describes the new prompt guidance

criteria.action: describe in docs/cli.md (section "What the model may and may not do") and in docs/model-usage.md that the system prompt now includes each tool's guidelines, prefers read_file/search_files/find_files/list_files for reading, searching, finding and listing, and limits the shell to git and the build/test toolchain
criteria.contract: Both files contain the words "Tool guidelines" and "search_files" in that description, and `make check` exits 0

execution_paths.title: A shell phase gets the guidelines and the preference line

steps.action: runs the fix tool against an issue, which starts the codefix analyse phase through agentrun.Runner
selects read_file, search_files, find_files, list_files and execute, and adds the discouraging sentence to execute's description
registers the selected tools plus submit_analysis and appends toolsNote(registered) to the phase's system prompt
renders the tool list, the read-only preference line and the de-duplicated guidelines section, with the search-over-execute guideline once and submit_analysis's guideline included
receives a system prompt that contains the guidelines section and the preference line

execution_paths.title: A phase without a shell keeps the no-shell sentence and gets its submit guidelines

steps.action: runs the triage tool, which starts a phase through agentrun.Runner with read-only file tools and no shell
drops every guideline that mentions execute from the selected tools
renders the tool list, the "There is no shell…" sentence and a guidelines section with no preference line and no search-over-execute guideline
receives a system prompt that contains the triage submit tool's guideline and no execute guidance
